title: Oregon revenue forecast shows about $245M more for 2027-29
summary: The November forecast raised expected 2027-29 general fund revenue by roughly $245M, driven by gains among higher-income Oregonians; state economists cautioned that such booms tend to correct. The forecast is the last one before Kotek's Dec 1 budget.
key_facts: ~$71M corporate kicker goes to K-12 by law
note: Summary carried over from the 2026-11-19 research brief; check against the article before reuse.

title: Kotek unveils policy proposals for a second term
summary: Kotek's reelection platform has four pillars, one of them improving K-12 schools. School items include reaching the national average for instructional time by the end of a second term, cutting chronic absenteeism, tougher diploma requirements, literacy, universal preschool and revisiting enrollment-based funding. The plan did not say how the school goals would be paid for.
key_facts: Instructional time to national average by end of second term
note: Summary carried over from the 2026-11-19 research brief; check against the article before reuse.

title: Gov. Kotek promises changes to Oregon schools in second term
summary: Post-election coverage of Kotek's school agenda for her second term, restating her outcome goals; she made no specific funding commitment.

title: Kotek's priorities after reelection
summary: Interview-based look at Kotek's second-term priorities. On schools she declined to commit to how she would pay for her goals and repeated her opposition to using one-time reserves for ongoing costs.
note: Summary carried over from the 2026-11-19 research brief; check against the article before reuse.

title: Gov. Tina Kotek's plan for ambitious academic goals gets scrutiny, then hesitant support from Board of Education
summary: The State Board of Education approved SB 141 achievement targets due in 2029-30 (e.g. 8th-grade math proficiency from 29% to 52%), with escalating interventions for districts that miss them. ODE's director said the targets need no new money; some board members pushed back.
note: Summary carried over from the 2026-11-19 research brief; check against the article before reuse. URL from an aggregator listing; free copy via Salem Reporter.

title: Oregon education funding committee recommends increasing school spending by $2.5B to $5B
summary: The Quality Education Commission's 2026 report estimates schools need nearly $2.5B more to maintain current service in 2027-29 and nearly $5B more to meet new accountability and attendance targets. Personnel costs drive most K-12 spending.

quotes.speaker: QEC report, as quoted by OPB

title: Kotek's executive order to reset student instructional time fans flames in Portland
summary: Kotek's executive order bars districts from cutting instructional time and requires restoring 2024-25 levels by 2027-28, without new funding attached.
note: Summary carried over from the 2026-11-19 research brief; check against the article before reuse.

title: Calls to tap state education reserves continue as PPS proposes hundreds of layoffs
summary: Pressure to use the Education Stability Fund grew as PPS proposed layoffs; Kotek said she did not expect additional school money beyond the current budget.
note: Summary carried over from the 2026-11-19 research brief; check against the article before reuse.

title: Facing a $65 million deficit, Portland Public Schools asks the state to step in
summary: PPS leaders asked the state to use $500M of the roughly $1B Education Stability Fund to buy down PERS rates for districts statewide. Using the fund requires a governor's emergency declaration and a three-fifths legislative vote.
note: Summary carried over from the 2026-11-19 research brief; check against the article before reuse.

title: School district begs state for bailout
summary: PPS CFO Michelle Morrison said the requested PERS relief would cut the district's $65M gap to about $42.7M.
note: Summary carried over from the 2026-11-19 research brief; check against the article before reuse.

title: Lawmakers weigh tax increases, reserve funds as PPS faces $65M budget gap
summary: At a Nov 12 forum, Rep. Tammy Carpenter suggested the Education Stability Fund as a bridge and said she has filed revenue proposals; Rep. Zach Hudson expects revenue bills in 2027 without giving a figure or timeline.
note: Summary carried over from the 2026-11-19 research brief; check against the article before reuse.

title: Gov. Kotek says her next Oregon budget will prioritize summer learning programs
summary: At a press event at Faubion School in Northeast Portland, Kotek said education and summer learning would be priorities in her 2027-29 budget, while warning of difficult choices. The article notes Education Stability Fund conditions and pushback from the teachers' union and district leaders.
key_facts: Exact date not on page (remarks made on a Tuesday); find it

quotes.text: We have a lot to figure out before I get my budget up in December.
quotes.speaker: Gov. Tina Kotek

quotes.text: my budget will be prioritizing education and particularly summer investments again
quotes.speaker: Gov. Tina Kotek

title: Governor proposes $11.36 billion State School Fund for 2025-27
summary: Kotek proposed an $11.36B State School Fund for 2025-27, an 11% increase; the 2023-25 SSF was $10.2B. The 2024 QEM estimated a $12.7B SSF was needed.

title: Gov. Kotek tells PPS leaders to 'take the time to get this right' regarding proposed school closures
summary: Describes Kotek's Tuesday (Oct 13) letter to Superintendent Kimberlee Armstrong and Board Chair Eddie Wang: she relayed families' shock and confusion and urged PPS to slow down, but did not ask the district to withdraw its closure plans.
key_facts: Asked PPS to take its time; not to retract

title: Kotek urges PPS to cut administrative costs before moving to close schools
summary: At a press availability Kotek said PPS should show what it has cut and how closures help students before deciding; KATU reports she rejected tapping one-time state reserves and signaled the state may rethink enrollment-based funding.

quotes.text: Portland needs to do everything it possibly can to cut administrative costs and other things before it talks about closing schools.
quotes.speaker: Gov. Tina Kotek

title: Governor Kotek issues executive order prohibiting school districts from reducing school days to cut costs
summary: On EO 26-06. Reports that an FAQ released with the order suggested Kotek was open to using the Education Stability Fund to help districts with one-time budget issues so they could comply.
key_facts: EO FAQ: open to ESF for one-time compliance costs

title: Powerful Lawmakers Say They Don't Anticipate Tapping Education Stability Fund This Year
summary: At a May 7 school funding forum hosted by Community + Parents for Public Schools, Ways and Means co-chairs Sen. Kate Lieber and Rep. Tawna Sanchez said they saw no reason to tap the Education Stability Fund this year. Lieber said there had been no cuts to school funding, so the fund wasn't needed, and warned against one-time money for ongoing costs. Sanchez said worse years are coming as federal H.R. 1 shifts social-service costs to the state in 2027-29 and 2029-31. Both pointed to revenue reform as the long-term answer.
key_facts: Access needs economic triggers or a governor's emergency declaration, plus a three-fifths vote

quotes.text: If you use one-time money to pay for ongoing expenses, then you're still going to have a cliff.
quotes.speaker: Sen. Kate Lieber

quotes.text: It's actually not raining quite yet. The hurricane has not hit yet.
quotes.speaker: Rep. Tawna Sanchez

title: To square Oregon's budget, lawmakers say many state agency jobs must go unfilled
summary: Ways and Means co-chairs briefed reporters on the 2026 rebalance. Lieber said the transportation department and the general fund will both need long-term fixes through sustainable revenue in the years ahead, and warned the deficit would worsen because of federal changes.

title: Oregon lawmakers consider overhaul of decades-old school funding model
summary: Rep. Ricki Ruiz described a proposal to replace the Quality Education Model, in place since 1999, with a funding approach tied to student outcomes and accountability, citing an independent review that questioned how the model is calculated.

quotes.text: Every year we have this debate of what is adequate funding for public schools in the state of Oregon
quotes.speaker: Rep. Ricki Ruiz

quotes.text: We're not repeating the same cycle and expecting different results
quotes.speaker: Rep. Ricki Ruiz

title: OR students, advocates press lawmakers for more school funding despite falling enrollment
summary: PPS students, board members and Superintendent Armstrong lobbied at the Capitol and asked lawmakers to consider the Education Stability Fund. KATU reports Rep. Ricki Ruiz said discussions about possibly accessing reserves were ongoing and lawmakers would keep monitoring (paraphrase; no direct quote).

title: What does the primary's biggest legislative upset say about the state of Oregon politics?
summary: Sen. Janeen Sollman lost the May 19 Democratic primary for Senate District 15 to Myrna Munoz in a race centered on data centers, with several groups that usually back Democratic incumbents supporting the challenger.
key_facts: Sollman leaves office when her term ends in January 2027

title: Oregon lawmakers hint at major changes to school funding in 2027
summary: The Senate confirmed Kotek's Quality Education Commission nominees 16-12; Sen. Sollman joined all Republicans voting no, objecting to process. The article notes Sollman and Rep. Ruiz led an unsuccessful 2026 effort to overhaul the funding model, and Sen. Lew Frederick said he expects significant changes to the QEM in 2027.
key_facts: SB 1555 overhaul did not pass in 2026

quotes.text: The question before us isn't whether these are good people, it's about process.
quotes.speaker: Sen. Janeen Sollman
